clue.text: Merry individual in charge of rowers?

definitions.meaning: slightly drunk, having had a drink too many
a cox sits facing the eight oarsmen of a racing boat, one person over the crew of eight

explanation.surface: Asks who keeps a jolly crew of oarsmen in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for tipsy is read literally: the coxswain is the extra person set over an eight-oar crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having drunk one more than is wise, so tipsy and cheerful.

clue.text: The M25, say -—- what's said about small section?

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the spoken word encloses the small piece

parts.note: oral describes what is spoken rather than written
a bit is a small part or section

explanation.surface: Asks what people say about a short stretch of London's ring motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London, the standard British example of a road that circles a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circling a city is called this, and the M25 is the classic British instance.

clue.text: Faux pas made by enfant terrible losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an enfant terrible is a little terror, an unruly young person

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by a notorious young rebel who has lost his composure.
explanation.definitionFit: A faux pas is a social blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Good outlook here in struggle with US Military Academy?

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
the US Military Academy at West Point is often known simply as the Point

explanation.surface: Suggests a scenic lookout found during a contest with American army cadets.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the shortening of West Point to its nickname, the Point. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantage spot is a place from which there is a good view.

clue.text: Isle of Wight resort trip announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the word for a trip is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a ride is a short journey or trip

explanation.surface: A holiday trip to a seaside town is being advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast; this is its main ferry town.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is a seaside resort and ferry port on the Isle of Wight's north coast.

clue.text: A very powerful man, he controls boxing clubs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to rule is to control or govern
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: A strongman who runs the local boxing gyms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport but is the container signal; 'clubs' is the card suit, not gyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Greek hero of the twelve labours is a byword for a man of great strength.

clue.text: Stops blowing top and relaxes

indicators.note: blowing its top means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Someone who stops losing their temper calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like an idiom for losing one's temper but signals removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax tension is to loosen or lessen it, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Gullible type flourishing? Blow me!

parts.note: green describes something growing vigorously and fresh
a horn is something one blows, read as an instruction to blow it

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a naive person doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' looks like a mild British oath of surprise; it is read as 'thing that you blow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive, inexperienced newcomer easily taken in is a tenderfoot of this kind.

clue.text: Violent storm encountered on the way over — bother!

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so the word for encountered is read backwards

parts.note: met means came across someone, as on a journey
a pest is a nuisance, something that bothers

explanation.surface: A traveller curses on running into foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountered on the way' reads as part of the storm story, but it simply gives a word for came across; 'over' then turns it round before the word for bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a gale with rain, a severe storm.

clue.text: One serving Arthur during drunken spree

indicators.note: during means within, so one word sits inside the drinking binge

parts.note: a bender is a drinking binge
Art is the short form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: Arthur goes on a binge while helping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One serving' sounds like a phrase about Arthur but is the definition: someone serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman's job is to serve drinks to customers.

clue.text: Leader of Socialist party in power

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a team is a group or party working together

explanation.surface: The head of a socialist party holds office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'power' reads as political office but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour drives engines, so the word is used for driving force, as in full speed ahead.

clue.text: Stumbles across opening in hedgerow, exposing insects

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the word for stumbles stretches around the letter

parts.note: trips means stumbles

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone trips over a gap in a hedge and disturbs the bugs living there.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tiny winged bugs that damage crops, the word being both singular and plural.

clue.text: Canine with us, barking, is a source of annoyance

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dog barking with us around is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' fits the dog but is the anagram signal; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest or bother is something that irritates.

clue.text: Calm, one policeman breaking cover

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the pair goes inside the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover
I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is military police, a policeman

explanation.surface: A single officer calmly blows a suspect's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and still water, or a serene style, is described as tranquil in this way.

clue.text: Smuggled alcohol? That's foolish talk

definitions.meaning: illicitly distilled or smuggled liquor, the question mark admitting it is often merely illegal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bootleg spirits and nonsense, like the light of the night sky.

clue.text: One learning nautical skills at Scouse resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone learning to sail at a Liverpool seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is re-sort, an anagram signal. Scouse means from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the maritime branch of the Scout movement learns boating and seamanship.

clue.text: Wretched rascal met wise guy

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A miserable rogue came across a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who is irritatingly clever is a wise guy.

clue.text: Telephone system popular company installed in Trinity, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside another word

parts.note: Trinity is the summer term at Oxford and some other universities

explanation.surface: A firm puts a phone network into a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity' looks like a college but is an academic term, the summer one at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal phone or speaker link within a building lets rooms talk to one another.

clue.text: Fair game at home? Good

parts.note: a sport is a game
in means at home

explanation.surface: Asks whether hunting quarry at home is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Fair' is the definition and 'game' gives SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous and fair-minded behaviour, as in a gentlemanly gesture, is described this way.

clue.text: Odds against snooker foul producing something advantageous?

indicators.note: against means next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
an in-off is a foul in snooker when the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a foul in snooker leading to a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the betting term for odds at the off. 'producing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary benefit or by-product arising from a larger venture is a beneficial offshoot.

clue.text: Vigorous blow catching a protruding stomach

indicators.note: catching means holding, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: a punch is a vigorous blow

explanation.surface: A hard punch lands on someone's big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot belly is a large stomach that sticks out.

clue.text: Fish, shad, missing head and tail

indicators.note: missing its head means the first letter of the word is gone

parts.note: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail, so as a verb tail means dock

explanation.surface: A fish with its head and tail cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head and tail' looks like one instruction for shad, but 'and' is a link: 'tail' alone gives DOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod.

clue.text: Decidedly trendy suit

parts.note: in means fashionable
spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit is definitely in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' reads as clothing but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts or to a marked degree, emphatically.

clue.text: In a Swiss canton, cuckoo-clock originally made of gold

parts.note: Uri is one of the cantons of Switzerland

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cuckoo clock in a Swiss region was first made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word introducing the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Latin for gold, the adjective means golden or of that metal.

clue.text: Lacking common sense, boss employing Greek character

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the letter pair goes inside

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dim manager hires a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests an employer but is a raised knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone foolish or dim lacks good sense.

clue.text: End of fighting announced for knight, perhaps

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the word for an end to fighting is heard

parts.note: peace is the end of fighting

explanation.surface: A knight proclaims the end of hostilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' sounds medieval but is the chess knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is one of the chessmen on the board, an example of a game counter.

clue.text: Old article about British port

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old item concerning a British harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is a harbour on the Scottish west coast, a gateway to the islands.

clue.text: Willow, very large one approaching centre of Caterham

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for very large
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the centre of an even-length word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A huge willow tree nears the middle of a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Caterham is a town in Surrey; its middle pair of letters ends the answer. 'approaching' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This willow species has pliant twigs used in basketwork.

clue.text: Foreign gentleman in conspiracy takes devious role

parts.note: a cabal is a secret plotting group, a conspiracy

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish gent in a plot plays an underhand part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a gentleman or horseman, used in English of a Spanish gentleman.

clue.text: Nice fellow councillor blocking attempt to obtain novel

parts.note: a man from Nice, the city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the way, so the councillor sits inside the other word

parts.note: to seek is to try to get

explanation.surface: A pleasant local politician hinders a man's efforts to get a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective but is the French city. The novel is by Daphne du Maurier.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1941 romance by Daphne du Maurier is a work of fiction set in Cornwall.
